question: Does natural role adaptation improve jointly correct actor/patient answers across meaning-preserving forms and role reversal, beyond source adapters, on new constructed items?

questions.actor_acted: Who acted on the other person?

prompt: Fixed chat system says answer with one candidate name; user gives sentence, alphabetically fixed candidate list, and question. Both event directions are included to balance candidate position.
answer_measure: Greedy next-token answer must decode to exactly the gold name; invalid outputs count wrong. Candidate actor-vs-patient next-token logit margin is reported separately.
event_level_measure: Both roles correct under both wordings across all four meaning-preserving forms; both participant directions evaluated as separate records but paired within unordered pair/verb.
omitted_sentence_control: For each event/role/wording prompt, replace sentence with [omitted] while keeping both candidate names; candidate margin only.
primary_comparison: Within each of two matched starts, natural-role adapter minus its source adapter on event-level exact correctness. Report individual starts and six pair groups; no claim of independent datasets.
success_screen: An exploratory positive requires at least four additional jointly correct events of 36 in each matched start, no more than two fewer active-form correct prompts per start, and a sentence-present margin gain larger than omitted-sentence margin gain. Otherwise do not claim robust transfer.
limits: One Qwen0.5B model family; synthetic templates; no human natural-language confirmation; source and natural adapters already selected in earlier work. This is a new test set, not a blind paper-level replication.
